samples.summary: `VERIFIER_FAILURE_KINDS` still enumerates only the three old kinds, so a verifier session killed by a drained pool tallies as `unknown`
samples.evidence: The diff creates one shared predicate for the never-ran kinds (`sessionNeverRan`, scripts/agent/ask.mjs:670) but the parallel kind list at scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:2453 — `Object.freeze({ "api-error": "apiError", limit: "limit", "no-output": "noOutput" })` — was not updated. `recordVerifierFailure` (review-panel.mjs:2444) copies `err.kind` verbatim, so a verifier session that throws `poolExhaustedError` (`kind: "pool-exhausted"`) lands in the `unknown` bucket at review-panel.mjs:2481, and the operator-facing tally at scripts/agent/metrics.mjs:744 prints `0 api-error, 0 turn-limit, 0 no-output` while `total` counts it. Same outage, two different reports depending on how many credentials the run had — exactly the inconsistency the diff's own rationale argues against. Fix belongs on the new/adjacent code: either add `"pool-exhausted"` to the map (folding it into `apiError`, or a new bucket) or key the map off the shared predicate.

samples.summary: Newly tagging a drained pool as infra changes an out-of-diff eval consumer from "scored" to "aborted"
samples.evidence: Because `lensInfraReason` now returns a string for `kind: "pool-exhausted"`, `panelEntry.infraError` is set, and `scripts/agent/eval/run.mjs:288-294` turns that item into `status: "error", reason: "infra"`. `assertItemsOk` (scripts/agent/eval/reliability.mjs:430-445, called from `reliabilityOf` at :801) then ABORTS the whole K-run reliability computation for any non-`ok` item — see the pinned behaviour in eval/reliability.test.mjs:660-664. Before this change a drained-pool leg produced an ordinary (bogus-blocker) item and scored. The new behaviour is arguably the honest one, but it is a behaviour change to a consumer the diff does not touch and no test or note covers it; an eval replay that previously completed under credential contention will now fail closed at scoring time.

samples.summary: `POOL_EXHAUSTED` added to the closed vocabulary but the fix-effort advice renderer does not recognise it, so it advises "a human should take a look" for a wait-for-reset outage
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/metrics.mjs:878-886 branches on `outcome.code === "USAGE_LIMIT"` to print the "account session limit — comment `@claude fix` again after the window resets" advice, then falls through to `outcome.kind === "limit"` / `outcome.retryable` / "Not retryable as-is; a human should take a look.". The new `POOL_EXHAUSTED` code (redact.mjs:262) means exactly the wait-or-rotate remedy, but matches none of those branches, so a drained pool renders the least actionable advice. Reachability is unconfirmed: the fix-agent `outcome` is built by `classifyFixResult` from a session result message (metrics.mjs:1095, session-job-summary.mjs:87), not from a thrown `poolExhaustedError`, so this may be unreachable today — confirming it needs a trace of whether any `outcome` consumer is ever fed an error object carrying `code`.

samples.summary: A pool drained mid-round after detection succeeded still publishes as a normal review round — the never-ran classification is applied only in `allSamplesFailedError`
samples.evidence: `sessionNeverRan` is consulted at exactly one place (scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:1770). If detection samples succeed and then every verifier session dies on the drained pool, `verifyFinding`'s catch feeds `recordVerifierFailure` (review-panel.mjs:2444) which only tallies a `{kind,status}` pair; no `infraError` is set on the panel entry, so the round counts toward MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS, the fixer runs, and biased-to-keep findings reach the gate unverified. This is pre-existing and identical for `api-error`, so the diff breaks nothing — but it is the remaining path that reaches the gate without passing the new classification, and worth stating since the diff's stated goal is one predicate for "the reviewer never ran".
